description: What the project started by editor_run has printed, as entries with a severity: the errors and warnings the engine reported, each with where it happened, and everything else as info. For a run the editor plays the reports come from the game itself, through the runtime addon, since the editor's debugger relays what a game prints and not what it reports; a played game without the runtime addon answers here with its prints alone, with errorsUnread true and no clean, since what it raised reaches nothing here. A run answers with counts and a verdict: clean is true when no error was reported, and warnings, counted beside it, do not make it false. heldAt is three answers: null for a run this server knows is not held, running or over, an object for one it knows is held at a breakpoint, whether the adapter said so or the runtime did by accepting a connection and never answering, and absent with heldUnknown beside it for a server that connected to the debugger after the stop and has no runtime to ask, since the adapter reports a stop only to the sessions connected when it happened. A run that has quit still answers here, with running false and its exit code, until the next one starts; a run ended by a signal has no exit code, and exitSignal names the signal instead. A run this server started also answers with transcript, the file both its streams are written to: uncapped, written while the run is going, and the thing to read or tail for a long run rather than the engine's own log, which every engine start rotates away. Read the file for output and this answer for state: endedBy says whether gdharness ended the run, and a transcript that has stopped growing is a run between prints rather than a run that is over. running is asked of the operating system whenever there is a process to ask about, which is every run this server started and every editor-played run whose game announced its runtime. For an editor-played run that never announced, there is no process id here and running is the editor's answer, which can lag: one reported a game as playing fifteen seconds after its process was ended from outside. editor_status names that game under runtimes, which does not depend on the editor answering. op: "editor" answers about the editor itself instead, which is a different log and the only way anything here can read what an editor printed: its console reaches no plugin, so the addon cannot scrape it, and an editor gdharness opened is asked for a log file as it starts. That covers the whole session from the editor's first line, where the output worth reading usually is, since the class cache, the plugins and the language server speak before any harness connects. It answers counts with no clean, since an editor neither passes nor fails, the entries in the order they were printed and, beside them under repeated, each message shape several lines share: how many, what varied in each slot of it and how many different values stood there, the first occurrence, and the ordinary lines above the group, found by walking back past the group rather than by counting lines. An editor somebody opened by hand has no console here and is refused saying so rather than answered empty, because an editor that printed nothing and an editor nobody captured are not the same thing. startedAt is when the run began and elapsedMs how long it has been going; for a run that is over, endedAt is when it ended and elapsedMs how long it ran, and both are left out when nobody saw the end, as for a game closed in the editor or a run picked up from a note written before ends were recorded. Operations: run: What the game a run is playing has printed, which is everything described above; editor: What the editor itself has printed, from its first line, each of the engine's progress bars as one line saying how far an unfinished task got. With no editor connected, the console the last editor gdharness opened here left, ending where a crashed one stopped. Default run. The tool reference in the gdharness skill, and the site, say what every field of the answer means.

before.description: How many lines above a repeated group to carry with it, counting only lines that are not themselves part of a group. Default 3. The line that explains a wall of identical errors is the last ordinary line above it, so this walks past the wall rather than a fixed distance back. Only for op editor.

contains.description: Only entries mentioning this text, matched against everything the run has printed rather than against the entries this answer would otherwise carry: a line is found however much was printed after it.

cpu.description: Also answer with cpuSeconds, the processor time the run has used. Default false, because asking costs a subprocess. Worth it when elapsedMs is climbing and nothing is being printed: processor time standing still is a run that has stopped doing anything, rather than one that is slow. Only for op run.

limit.description: The most entries to answer with, newest kept. Identical entries come back as one, at the first of them, with times saying how many were printed, so the limit counts distinct entries. Default 200, and omitted says how many distinct matching entries that left out. A run long enough to pass it needs this raised, not just filtered: filtering narrows what counts as matching, and the newest of those is still all one answer carries.

projectPath.description: The project whose output you mean to read. It picks nothing, since this reads the one run or editor this server holds, and a call naming another project than that one's is refused rather than answered with output from a different game.

severity.description: The least severe entry to include. Default info, which is everything.

sinceLastCall.description: Only entries this has not already answered with at this severity. Default false. Measured per severity floor and not across them, so polling for errors leaves the rest of the output for a later read rather than consuming it, and a read with contains is a search over the whole run and consumes nothing. Only for op run.

name: editor_output
title: Game and editor output
